Playbook.name: SWIFT — Administrative or Attacker Tooling Executed on a SWIFT Server - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A process (4688) ran on a SWIFT server that matches administrative or attacker tooling (PsExec, PowerShell, credential/recon tools, etc.). SWIFT servers should run only a tightly-controlled software set. Triage: sanctioned SWIFT administration, or attacker tooling on a payment server?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Any unexpected tooling on a SWIFT server threatens the payment system - the highest-impact banking asset.

Assets.AssetType: SWIFT Alliance payment servers (saa*, hq-sw-app*, hq-swift*)

LogSources.LogSource: Windows Security on SWIFT servers - logs-system.security-*

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing on SWIFT hosts (verified live: saa76dr, hq-sw-app-p, hq-swift-accs-p, saa72live, hq-swift-web-p). SWIFT servers are the highest-value payment assets - any anomaly is high priority.

Signal.Name: Administrative or Attacker Tooling Execu
Signal.Details: process on a SWIFT host matching admin/attacker tooling.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the tooling on the SWIFT server is sanctioned administration or attacker activity.

Step.name: Tooling/process activity on the SWIFT server
Step.Purpose: The process, parent and account reveal sanctioned admin vs attacker tooling on this restricted asset.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | WHERE process.name RLIKE "(?i)(psexec|powershell|pwsh|cmd|wmic|net1?|reg|mimikatz|procdump|rubeus|certutil|bitsadmin|nc|ncat).*" | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.parent.name, user.name, process.command_line | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: On a SWIFT server, ANY PsExec/credential-tool/download-tool is high concern. Sanctioned admin uses a known jump-host/account under change control. Read command_line for intent; an unexpected account or tool is likely an incident.

Step.name: Logon context on the SWIFT server
Step.Purpose: Where the session originated (jump host vs unexpected source) distinguishes sanctioned admin from intrusion.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code == "4624" AND winlog.event_data.LogonType IN ("2","3","10") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS logons = COUNT(*), users = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), types = VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType) BY src | SORT logons DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: A logon from an approved SWIFT jump host by an authorised operator is sanctioned. A logon from an unexpected source, or a non-SWIFT account, preceding the tooling is intrusion.

Node.Condition: Attacker/credential/download tooling on the SWIFT server, or tooling from an unexpected source/account.
Node.Result: True Positive (Intrusion on SWIFT Server - CSP incident process, IR)

Node.Condition: Sanctioned SWIFT administration using an approved tool/account under change control.
An admin using a non-standard-but-legitimate tool without a change record.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-SWIFT-PROC, INV-02-SWIFT-LOGON to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the change/admin; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: Attacker tooling on a SWIFT payment server.

SOCAction.Item: Invoke the SWIFT CSP incident process; isolate the server; preserve evidence; review payments for fraud; open IR.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A non-standard admin tool used without change control.

SOCAction.Item: Require change control; document; add the tool to the allowlist if approved.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the SWIFT server; SWIFT anomalies are high priority.
If unauthorised, isolate per the SWIFT CSP incident process.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the SWIFT server per the CSP incident process; preserve evidence; engage the SWIFT/payments team; open IR.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce SWIFT CSP controls: restricted access, MFA/jump-host, allowlisted software, segregation from the general network.

QualityChecks.Check: SWIFT servers are in-scope for the SWIFT Customer Security Programme - treat every anomaly as high priority and involve the payments team.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: SWIFT server isolated per CSP; payments reviewed; IR recorded.
